# axiolid-hidden-lines

Exact scalar hidden-line drawings of triangle meshes in orthographic views.

## Overview

The exact scalar provider for `MeshHiddenLines` (ADR 0090): the visible and
hidden pieces of the boundary, silhouette and crease edges of triangle
meshes in an orthographic view. Visibility is decided exactly in the view's
affine frame, with the interval filter first and dyadic big integers when it
cannot decide; no tolerance enters a decision, and the output endpoints are
the exact points rounded once. It refuses what it cannot decide with a typed
error that names the mesh. Candidate pairs are found in an `axiolid-spatial` BVH over view-space boxes
(worst case still edges times triangles); the examined pairs are bounded by
`max_candidate_pairs`. A
near clipping plane that cuts a `Solid` mesh leaves a cap that occludes, decided
by exact ray parity with a symbolic perturbation of the image point; a face of a
cut solid in the plane needs no special case. A solid wholly beyond the plane is
removed.
It does not draw perspective views, exact B-rep edges or smooth silhouettes.

## Changes

Latest release, 0.1.2 (2026-10-29):

### Changed

- Candidate triangles for an edge, and the cap triangles of a cut solid, come from an `axiolid-spatial` BVH over view-space boxes instead of a linear scan. The predicate, the candidate set, its ascending order and `candidate_pairs` are unchanged (#138). Wall clock from `scenario/hidden-lines` (`cargo bench -p axiolid-benchmark --bench scenario -- hidden-lines`, which times the BVH and the linear scan, `ScanHiddenLines`, on each case; a loaded shared machine, so read these as ranges), linear scan / BVH: isometric 20x20 boxes 412 / 389 ms (a reviewer's run: 459 / 426), cut plan 20x20 174 / 140 ms (117 / 100; very noisy), isometric 50x50 3.34 / 2.52 s (3.62 / 2.88), cut plan 50x50 1.59 / 0.76 s (1.67 / 0.82). The gain is small at 400 boxes, because exact evaluation of the candidates dominates there, and 25-30% (isometric) to about 50% (cut plan) at 2,500.
